text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Central bank removes 21 percent ceiling on interest rates.
- Post and telecommunications workers have vowed to resist any attempt by government to privatise their state-owned companies.
- Installation of the computerised central clearing system at the stock exchange is likely to be completed next month.
- Cement manufacturers have finally abandoned a campaign to be allowed to import gypsum, and are now using local gypsum.

- Shell Petroleum Development Company has designed a scheme which will utilise all gas flared from oil production installations by 2008. Under the scheme one billion cubic metres a day of associated gas would be utilised.
- Accountants have advised the government to set up a serious fraud office to check, detect and prosecute fraudsters on a permanent basis.
- Two multinational oil companies, Shell and Chevron, have expressed interest in a 260 billion naira project to build a gas pipeline running from Nigeria through neighbouring Benin and Togo to Ghana.
